classes.name: Sovietul Suprem al RSS Moldovenești (Parlamentul de legislatura XII, 1990)
classes.name_en: Supreme Soviet of the Moldavian SSR elected in 1990 (first Parliament)
classes.note: First competitive election: 380 deputies in single-member districts by two-round majority in February and March 1990; the body proclaimed independence and served as Parliament until 1994.
classes.disposition_reason: The CEC of 1989-1993 published no results that survive online; district returns sit only in the 1990 official gazette and the Supreme Soviet's records, which have not been located.

dates.quote: This Central Electoral Commission ... was in charge with conducting the parliamentary elections since 1990
dates.note: First round 25 February 1990, runoffs in March.

classes.name: Sovietul Suprem al RSS Moldovenești (1941-1985)
classes.name_en: Supreme Soviet of the Moldavian SSR (1941-1985)
classes.note: Single-candidate Soviet elections in single-member districts, every four years from 1941 (five from 1979).
classes.disposition_reason: Uncontested single-list elections whose district returns are only in Soviet-era gazettes; no official publication is online.

classes.name: Sovietele locale de deputați ai poporului (RSSM)
classes.name_en: Local soviets of the Moldavian SSR
classes.note: District, city, and village soviets elected by Soviet single-candidate rules, last in 1990 with the Supreme Soviet; replaced by the councils elected in April 1995.
classes.disposition_reason: No official publication of local soviet returns is online.

classes.name: Alegeri prezidențiale
classes.finest_note: Polling-station workbooks for 2016 and 2024; result pages for 2020.
classes.note: Direct two-round election (majority of votes cast) in 1991 and 1996; Parliament elected the president from 2001 to 2012 (presedinte_parlament); the Constitutional Court restored direct election on 4 March 2016. Four-year term.

classes.name: Referendumuri în UTA Găgăuzia
classes.note: The local referendums of 5 March 1995 that fixed which localities joined the autonomy, and the regional vote of 2 February 2014 on foreign policy and secession, which Moldovan courts declared unlawful.
classes.disposition_reason: Results were published only by Gagauzia's own electoral commission, whose site did not answer from here; the 2014 vote was held against a court ban and has no national publication.

classes.name: Alegeri organizate de autoritățile de facto din stînga Nistrului
classes.name_en: Elections held by the de facto authorities of Transnistria
classes.disposition_reason: Held outside Moldovan law by an unrecognized administration; Moldova's own elections cover left-bank voters at special polling stations on the right bank, which the national classes already count.

classes.name: Alegeri indirecte (Prim-ministru, Președintele Parlamentului, președinții de raion, viceprimari)
classes.name_en: Indirect elections of the Prime Minister, Speaker, district presidents, and deputy mayors
classes.disposition_reason: Chosen by votes of Parliament or of the councils, not at a public election; the President is the only indirect office the census tracks (presedinte_parlament).

classes.name: Judecători
classes.disposition_reason: Judges are appointed by the President on the proposal of the Superior Council of Magistracy; none is elected by voters.

classes.name: Desemnarea candidaților de către partide
classes.disposition_reason: Parties choose their lists and candidates under their own statutes; the state runs no primary.

classes.name: Alegeri în organele URSS (Sovietul Suprem al URSS, Congresul deputaților poporului 1989)
classes.name_en: Elections to Soviet Union bodies held in the Moldavian SSR
classes.disposition_reason: Elections of all-Union bodies belong to the Soviet Union's history, not to Moldova's own institutions; Moldova boycotted the all-Union referendum of 17 March 1991.

classes.name: Sfatul Țării (1917-1918)
classes.disposition_reason: Its members were delegated by congresses, soviets, and national organizations of Bessarabia, not elected by voters; the interwar elections in Bessarabia were Romanian elections.
